source.quote: First off, well, we haven't really found a consistent gold farm that can truly move the needle here. On top of that, there's actually a few classic hinterlands farms that used to be available, which are just straight up gone now. We already talked about the ghost mushrooms, which have disappeared from the zone entirely, but that isn't where it stops. But more on that later. First up, let's head up to Genta Allore for the troll ruins, which to be fair, there's actually a few gold farms up here. Of course, the spider cave, which used to have ghost mushrooms, doesn't have those anymore. But there's still the spiders themselves inside, which are technically farmable, but they aren't on a hyperspawn, so we will have to wait in between clears of 8 to 12 spiders. On top of the slow clear time, they don't actually really have anything worth farming. They could of course drop some general greens or world drop epics. Technically the trade goods though between the crunchy spider legs which are worth about 45 silver, the large venom sacks about 1 silver, the small spider legs 13 silver, and the thick spider silk which is one of the cheapest spider silk variants at 43 silver. Farming these guys only works out to 63 gold per hour. Yeah, and since we have 200,000 gold left for the token, that would be 3,174 hours or 132 days of straight spider farming. So, spiders, aren't it? But that isn't all we have in genta allore, thankfully, because we do have something else here. Trolls. And in particular, trolls that drop wild vine. Now, this is a super low drop according to Wowhead, around.3%, which is for sure rare, but historically, groups that farm these guys will do a fiveman hyperspawn farm of the entire ruins and get tons of kills per hour. We're of course running a challenge on Goldie here and grouping for open world farms is out of the question, but we can still test it even if we get one every 300 kills. I can kill about 900 trolls per hour solo. And Wildbine is super valuable with a ticket price of 384 gold. Not bad. Most of the trolls do drop this according to Wowhead, but there is one troll archetype here that's a little more interesting. So, while farming Wildbine, we want to make sure to focus on the vile branch hide skinners. These guys can actually drop a rare recipe and maybe the best drop in the whole zone, the pattern for the iron feather breast plate. The recipe itself has an average list price of around 40,000 gold, while the crafted chest piece used with the leather wicking profession goes for about 5,000 gold. So, I will definitely want to farm up at least two of these drops. One just to sell as the recipe because 40,000 gold is pretty much as much as we have right now. and then one to send over to my one crafting alt, golden path, who just so happens to have leather working. So maybe not a death zone after all. Well, not so fast, cuz there's a problem. On testing this, even though Wowhead says the Wildvine is on the drop tables here, my data points otherwise. With thousands of trolls killed, zero wildvine. Looking into the forums, much like the ghost mushroom, when the zone scaling changed here in the hinterlands, the level bracket moved out of the Wild Vine drop range and with it removed yet another gold farm from the hinterlands. Not ideal. So, with that in mind, I'll call the trolls neutral. But that isn't all that Jimthaw Allore has. In addition to the leather working recipe, it has the second best drop in the zone as well. From the rare up in the top in the ruins, Mythreus the Enchanter. Now, this rare is the only one in the zone with a specific item that I feel is worth camping. The other rares are definitely worth killing for low value transmog. Well, this one drops the Chans Imperial Robes, a 20 to 40,000 gold transmog drop. So, we have two notable drops, at least so far in the zone, and we definitely want to camp this one. And since this is really the only mob worth camping in the zone, well, we need something to do in the meantime, which luckily this week's sponsor, Idle Obelisk Miner does just that, which if you're a fan of Goldbound, gold farming, and slow rewarding number go up progression, you're going to want to check this out.

source.quote: Unfortunately, the time forgotten farms of the hinterlands doesn't end with the wild vine or the ghost mushrooms. Far from it. Because back over at the Skull Rock Cave, the one that used to have ghost mushrooms, we have a few mob types roaming around. The Jade ooze and the green sludge. Historically, both of these mobs used to drop the ooloing bag, a familiar forgotten farm in the series. These are the same bags that used to drop in Swamp of Soros and Wetlands, but in retail, once we're past level 30 to 50 or so, they just stop dropping with mob and item scaling. And well, the hinterlands is no different. So, the ooloing bag, which is valuable because of the battle pet it can contain, the disgusting ooloing, is also lost to the zone. No matter how many of these little oozes we take out, we're not going to get the drop. It's not all bad news, though, because the cave does have some decent ore spawns throughout.

source.quote: Sure, the XP boost and rep boost is nice, but what is really wild for a challenge like Goldbound, is that every single mob we kill and quest we do, even in the Hinterlands and our unlocked zones, has a chance to give us a mysterious satchel. Inside the satchel, there's some odds and ends like warbound XP potions, but also gear. Now, this isn't transmog gear. It is all soulbound and actually can't be disenchanted. But there is a full mysterious set to be obtained. The big thing here, though, this gear scales to the level you were when you obtained the satchel. So, while we're running around in these super low-level zones at level 86, wearing item level 30 to 70 gear from our zones, these bags can drop blues and epics with gear item levels of 171 to 178. Pretty much light years better than any gear we can currently obtain in our zones. So, theoretically, we can try to get a full set of current content gear on Goldie while staying in our unlocked zones. So, let's get farming these satchels.

source.quote: There's a few ways that we can actually get them. First up, there is a bonus each day where the first couple of mobs that we kill just straight up give an epic satchel and the epic satchels always drop the epic gear. On top of that, while killing mobs in the open world or dungeons after that first drop of the day, we can just randomly get blue or epic satchels. Plus, doing quests can give satchels as well. So, let's go test these out. While farming these up though, it is worth noting that this won't be a direct instant gold income for Goldie. It's more of a futurep proofing for later zones where we may have mobs that are scaled way higher. We already had some strange scale like this in Alderman Legacy of Tier where mobs took quite a few hits to kill and well the red ridge spider no feeaster aka the red ridge raid boss which if we do get a full set we're definitely going for revenge. In a challenge like this we generally just don't know what will happen with scaling. It could change wildly with the next expansion and potential stat squishes in the future. So, while a limited time event like this is on, we really need to capitalize on it. With some farming and testing for these satchels under the belt, though, from a satchels per hour perspective, there is a very clear frontr runner. I first tested this out by just killing trolls over and over, and for an hour, we only procked two blue satchels. Not great. I even tried running some old dungeons like Alderman for high kills per hour to try to get some more satchels, but I got none. The real king here is the quests.

So, let's go test these out. While farming these up though, it is worth noting that this won't be a direct instant gold income for Goldie. It's more of a futurep proofing for later zones where we may have mobs that are scaled way higher. We already had some strange scale like this in Alderman Legacy of Tier where mobs took quite a few hits to kill and well the red ridge spider no feeaster aka the red ridge raid boss which if we do get a full set we're definitely going for revenge. In a challenge like this we generally just don't know what will happen with scaling. It could change wildly with the next expansion and potential stat squishes in the future. So, while a limited time event like this is on, we really need to capitalize on it. With some farming and testing for these satchels under the belt, though, from a satchels per hour perspective, there is a very clear frontr runner. I first tested this out by just killing trolls over and over, and for an hour, we only procked two blue satchels. Not great. I even tried running some old dungeons like Alderman for high kills per hour to try to get some more satchels, but I got none. The real king here is the quests.

Speaking of which, there is one thing that I do want to test farming out in this zone, especially since the Feast of Winter's Veil is coming up relatively soon. The owl beasts. Literally all over the zone are these moonkin looking owl beasts. There's two varieties though, the savage and the vicious. But for us, they're all the same because we're after one thing and one thing only, small eggs yet again. Now, the spawn area of these guys is so large that we don't really have to worry about respawn rates or routes. And we can use sprints and grappling hooks to get around quite well for some decent kills per hour. In fact, these guys pretty much cover the entire map, which is good and bad. It's good for farming them, but it does mean there isn't that much variety of mobs aside from these guys, trolls, and some oozes, and maybe some turtles on the beach. So, we definitely want to test them out when we're here because hey, there's not much else to farm in this zone. As far as the rates, I was thinking this would be a sub 1,000 gold per hour farm, but I'm honestly pleasantly surprised. We're pulling in about 350 small eggs per hour, which is way better than our original small egg farm in Red Ridge, but not as good as the Westfall or the Lock Madan ones. At current market prices, that's about 2,450 gold per hour just from the eggs. And who knows, the egg prices could spike a little bit in the future. Last Winter's Veil, they did go up to 100 gold each for a little bit and settled around 15 gold during the event, but did come back down to eight pretty quickly. Besides the small eggs here, we're really just getting some gray hollow wing bones and the odd green transmog. But hey, not a bad farm to mix into the zone. And we can use sprints and grappling hooks to get around quite well for some decent kills per hour. In fact, these guys pretty much cover the entire map, which is good and bad. It's good for farming them, but it does mean there isn't that much variety of mobs aside from these guys, trolls, and some oozes, and maybe some turtles on the beach. So, we definitely want to test them out when we're here because hey, there's not much else to farm in this zone. As far as the rates, I was thinking this would be a sub 1,000 gold per hour farm, but I'm honestly pleasantly surprised. We're pulling in about 350 small eggs per hour, which is way better than our original small egg farm in Red Ridge, but not as good as the Westfall or the Lock Madan ones. At current market prices, that's about 2,450 gold per hour just from the eggs. And who knows, the egg prices could spike a little bit in the future. Last Winter's Veil, they did go up to 100 gold each for a little bit and settled around 15 gold during the event, but did come back down to eight pretty quickly. Besides the small eggs here, we're really just getting some gray hollow wing bones and the odd green transmog. But hey, not a bad farm to mix into the zone. At least the small eggs still drop here, unlike a lot of other items in the zone. But with all that said, travelers, it's time to check the mailbox. And as you may know, there have been some pretty big announcements in WoW lately. and those well yeah they've moved their token price up from about 250,000 gold to darn near 300k at the moment. So let's hope for a pretty big mailbox clear. There's a lot of odds and ends here as far as trade goods, mostly from the zone, but also from Dark Moon which happened during this week. So, let's get this looted up.
